messages:
alex: Heads up — we need per-model & per-route latency/throughput SLO dashboards wired into Console for Hosted/Dedicated. Metrics: P50/P95/P99, TTFT (time-to-first-token), tokens/sec. Need runtime + infra inputs today. cc @janelle @rachel @kevin @tom

janelle: We can emit the tags/metrics from runtime. Plan to add labels: model_id, model_version, route, customer_tier, region, quantization, batch_size. Also add queue_time and ttft_ms. Will open PR with instrumentation by EOD.

rachel: Ingest side note: our OTLP pipeline currently aggregates by service only. We can accept extra labels but cardinality is a real concern. Proposals: (1) add model_major (e.g. 1.3 -> 1) to reduce versions, (2) route hashed id to keep label values bounded. We'll also need sampling/rollup rules for low-volume routes.

kevin: Dashboard UX wants templates per-route with the metrics you listed + these alert rules: p95 latency > threshold for 5m, ttft > threshold for 5m, tokens/sec drop > 30% vs baseline. We should show 1m/5m tokens/sec and live tokens/sec/tps. I'll prototype a Console widget.

tom: From product side, suggested default SLOs to start: hosted p95 <= 200ms, TTFT <= 100ms, tokens/sec >= 200 (tunable by model class). We'll iterate after we see real data. Need compare-to-baseline (pre-deploy) in dashboards.

janelle: Quick metric naming we'll use in runtime:
```
redwood.request.latency_ms{model,model_major,route_alias,region,customer_tier}
redwood.request.ttft_ms{...}
redwood.request.tokens_count{...}
redwood.request.batch_size{...}
```
Will also tag `fallback_route=true/false`, `deploy_id`, and `sample_rate` for sampled traces.

alex: Sounds good. Question: how do we defend against high-cardinality (many routes per customer) exploding our metrics backend? Also sensitive customers might want opt-out of route-level labels.

rachel: Two mitigations: 1) server-side rollups — for routes below X qps emit aggregated metric (rollup=true) instead of per-route, 2) bucket model_version into model_major as mentioned, 3) per-org cap on distinct route_alias values (e.g., 1000). Also allow customers to opt-in to full route labeling.

janelle: We'll add `route_alias` (short sha1-based id) as the primary label and keep full route path in logs only. That avoids long strings and reduces cardinality.

kevin: For rollout UX: the Console should accept `deploy_id` from runtime and attach SLO watches to canaries. Can runtime emit DEPLOY_ID env per process? Also we should auto-annotate dashboards with deploy metadata.

janelle: Yes — runtime can read DEPLOY_ID and tag requests. We'll include `model_variant` for fallbacks as well.

tom: Action items (owner):
- runtime: add metrics + tags + deploy_id (janelle)
- infra: extend metrics ingest + implement sampling/rollup rules + enforce route_alias caps (rachel)
- devex: build dashboard templates, alert rules, and rollout annotation UI (kevin)
- product: finalize SLO thresholds + rollout/annotation UX (tom)
Please paste PR/issue links here once opened.

alex: :thumbsup: I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow 10:00am to review the runtime PR and the dashboard prototype. Thanks everyone.

metrics-bot: Note: added temporary metric-cardinality alert (alerts will fire if unique label values increase > 20%/1h).

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: metrics-pipeline config change slated for 2026-01-17 02:00 UTC (tentative).
